newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pressure on Rwanda is key to Zaire aid - France.
newsitem.headline: Pressure on Rwanda is key to Zaire aid - France.

text.p: Rwanda is being pressured to rein in Tutsi rebels holding airports in Zaire where multinational forces will muster, a vital step in keeping the Zaire rescue mission free of violence, French officials said on Friday.
The officials said the first foreign troops would not reach the area until the middle of next week, delayed by the diplomatic preparations, rather than this weekend as initially predicted.
The United States and France have said their troops will be based at Goma and Bukavu airfields respectively in eastern Zaire, where supplies for a million starving refugees will pour in.
A foreign ministry official told reporters initial planning was that United States and Canadian troops would operate in the Goma area while European contingents would be based at Bukavu.
Both airfields are now in the hands of Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels who have warned they will shoot the French on sight and have also been cool about the arrival of other contingents.
France plans to contribute up to 2,000 troops to the Canadian-led mission, which could total 10,000 men following expected authorisation by the U.N. Security Council.

"As things now stand, the United Nations wants this operation to be a purely humanitarian one and avoid all violence although our forces will have a free hand to hit back vigorously if attacked," one senior French official told Reuters.

"That means we are not going to take those airfields by force. What is happening now is that international diplomatic pressure is being applied on Rwanda to tell the Banyamulenge, who do what Kigali tells them to do, to back off," said the official who asked not to be identified.

The French military have said they want to create a "security zone" around Bukavu airport which would stretch as far as the range of the heaviest calibre weapons that could be aimed at them by potential adversaries.
Another official indicated the French would limit their mission at Bukavu to guarding the airport and would not take part in convoy escort missions within Tutsi lines.
Rwanda and the Zairean Tutsis consider France an enemy, saying Paris' intervention in Rwanda in 1994 allowed Hutus responsible for the genocide of up to a million Tutsis to escape to Zaire.
France says its Operation Turquoise operation, with 2,500 troops, ended the genocide of Tutsis and that it is neutral in the centuries-old ethnic rivalry.

Speaking privately, several French officers said some top officers allied to the Banyamulenge included Zairean leftists who had been enemies of France since the mid-1970s when Paris parachuted troops into Shaba province to prevent it falling into the hands of Cuba-backed rebels.
